newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won hits new record low close on short cover.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won hits new record low close on short cover.

text.p: The won continued its slide against the dollar on Thursday, setting the third consecutive record closing low as banks rushed to cover their short dollar positions, traders said.

The won ended at a 844.90, down from an opening of 839.50. It widely fluctuated between 839.30 and a record intra-day low of 845. The closing rate was the lowest level since South Korea started interbank won/dollar trading in 1990, dealers said.
"Interbank dealers and importers are caught in short positions," said a western bank dealer. "Because there wasn't any intervention today, nobody knew where the ceiling was."
The previous record low was set on Wednesday, when the won/dollar rate closed at 839.40.
Traders said the won/dollar rate was likely to test 850 on Friday as the market was still short in dollars and more large scale importer settlements were due.
The central Bank of Korea set the base mid-rate for Friday at 842.80, compared to Thursday's 839.30.
